title: Sweden Caught Between Political Deadlock and a Recovery That Households… · 12 Oct
keywords: Sweden, Riksdag, Magdalena Andersson, Social Democrats, coalition talks, hung parliament, Swedish economy, Riksbank, inflation, CPIF, household costs, fuel tax, defence spending, EU, Nordic politics, government formation
notes: Sweden's centre-left bloc won the most seats in the Riksdag but has so far failed to convert that advantage into a stable government, leaving Social Democratic leader Magdalena Andersson in a second attempt to assemble a workable coalition. Meanwhile, an economy expected to grow by roughly 3% in 2026 is sending mixed signals: policymakers speak of recovery, but households still face rising prices and the Riksbank has warned that inflation risks are rebuilding. The two crises are inseparable, because whoever governs must immediately choose between household relief and fiscal restraint.
